R222.note: Regex only blocks malformed/special-character names; the real CWE-94 vector (attacker-chosen import target executing module-level code, e.g. plugin='os' or another installed/dangerous module) is still open since any syntactically valid identifier passes.

R223.note: full_clean() correctly triggers the model's validate_file_content validator before save; legitimate PDF/PNG/JPEG uploads still succeed (minor: an invalid upload now surfaces as an uncaught Django ValidationError/500 rather than a clean DRF 400, but that only affects the previously-vulnerable path).

R224.note: Correct parameterized SqlCommand with explicit SqlDbType; same query semantics for legitimate input.

R225.note: Correctly removes LIBXML_NOENT (the entity-substitution flag causing the finding) and adds LIBXML_NONET as defense in depth; well-formed submissions parse identically.

R226.note: Standard golang-jwt fix: type-asserts SigningMethodHMAC in keyFunc before returning the secret, closing the algorithm-confusion vector without affecting legitimate HMAC tokens.

R227.note: Overflow check (headerLen > UINT32_MAX - payloadLen) exactly identifies the wrap-around case and rejects only inputs that would have overflowed; no legitimate sum is rejected.

R228.note: The added 'authentication' only reads a raw, unverified gRPC metadata 'user-id' field as identity - the file itself notes zero interceptors/authentication exist, so an attacker can still delete any project by spoofing user-id to match the owner; the missing-authentication root cause is not actually closed, only a spoofable ownership check is added.

R229.note: Adds algorithms:['RS256'] matching the documented issuer algorithm; closes alg-confusion without affecting legitimate RS256 tokens.

R230.note: Correct HQL named-parameter binding via setParameter; identical query semantics for legitimate search terms.

R231.note: redis-py's set() correctly RESP-encodes key/value, closing the inline-protocol injection. But the function's return value silently changes from the raw socket reply bytes to a hardcoded literal "OK" on every call, and a Redis-side error now raises an exception instead of being returned as before - not disclosed in the write-up.

R232.note: Moves label into an HTML data attribute (Razor-encoded) and reads it via getAttribute in JS instead of embedding in a JS string literal; title keeps normal Razor encoding, refreshSeconds stays a numeric literal, label still exposed to JS - matches the stated contract.

R233.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword plus a dummy-hash timing mitigation is the correct API/pattern, but verified independently with bcryptjs and Python's bcrypt that the hardcoded hash for alice does NOT match "hunter2" - the fix silently breaks login for the case's own legitimate credentials, and the write-up presents the hash as equivalent to the original plaintext without flagging this.

R234.note: Correctly removes dynamic compilation (no safe sandbox exists) in favor of loading allowlisted precompiled DLLs, which is the appropriate CWE-94 remediation, but this is an openly-stated breaking API/contract change: existing callers supplying raw source code can no longer be served by this endpoint at all.

R235.note: Removes the is_staff queryset-widening branch so IsTicketOwner's owner-only rule applies uniformly, matching the file's own documented intended contract; no legitimate access is impacted beyond the unauthorized staff path being closed.

R236.note: Correct ODBC positional-parameter (?) query with AddWithValue; preserves the original LIKE wildcard search semantics.
